evals.name: granular-component-fix
evals.prompt: I fixed an ambiguous dot in a monitored repository row. Show me a granular before and after from the real local web app, using the same row, data, viewport, and browser session.
evals.expected_output: An element-level proof package captures the same real DOM element before and after, records source-state provenance and dimensions, and opens a self-contained comparison report.
assertions: Uses agent-browser composition without requiring an agent-browser source change
Captures the smallest useful DOM element with one stable selector
Keeps URL, data, session, viewport, and element boundary comparable
Records exact baseline and changed-state provenance
Returns the report plus individual before and after image paths

evals.name: responsive-layout-fix
evals.prompt: The mobile settings panel no longer overflows at 390px. Create visual proof from the web app at that exact viewport and make the layout-size change explicit.
evals.expected_output: A responsive element-level comparison preserves the 390px viewport, permits changed element dimensions only because layout size is the claim, and documents the exception.
assertions: Uses the same 390px viewport for baseline and changed captures
Captures the relevant panel rather than an unrelated full page
Allows different image dimensions only with an explicit size-change rationale
Records the route, selector, and source identities
Checks the generated report at a narrow viewport

evals.name: temporal-web-state
evals.prompt: Prove that the web loading placeholder no longer flickers before content appears. I want before and after evidence I can review in the browser.
evals.expected_output: The workflow recognizes that final stills cannot prove flicker and uses a video or ordered state sequence while retaining comparable element-level framing.
assertions: Does not claim that two settled screenshots prove flicker
Uses video or an ordered deterministic state sequence
Replays the same trigger and readiness conditions on both sides
Separates appearance evidence from temporal evidence
States the limits of the captured proof
